The real, unedited recording is further down . How it works The camera and the microphone both have to agree before saywhen listens. A camera alone cannot tell chewing from talking, and a microphone alone cannot tell who you are talking to. No camera? Option + Space on Mac or Alt + Space on Windows starts listening by hand. More in How saywhen works . Speaks developer Every row is a real case from the test suite in cleanup.rs . Add your own words for project names in Settings. Or say "scratch that". Enter is pressed only in apps you trust. Terminals and code editors are trusted by default. In chat, email and browsers, saywhen only types. If the app in front changes during the countdown, saywhen stops and types nothing. title: Questions people ask
text: Questions people ask Short answers first. Each one links to the page with the detail. Is saywhen free? Yes. saywhen is MIT licensed. There is no account, no subscription and no paid tier. The only optional cost is an AI endpoint if you turn on cloud clean-up, and the default is a local Ollama server. Does it work offline? Yes, after the speech model and the camera runtime have downloaded. The first setup needs the internet. After that, dictation, the camera gate, the check step and typing into other apps run on your computer. Optional cloud clean-up is off by default and sends text only, never audio or camera pictures. Does it record my camera or my voice? No. Camera frames are read in memory and thrown away. Audio is turned into text and discarded after transcription. The text you said is kept for 7 days in local history unless you turn history off. The one exception is the opt-in "Save recordings" switch in Diagnostics, which is off by default, turns itself off on restart and writes 16 kHz WAV files to the recordings/ folder. How is this different from Wispr Flow? Wispr Flow is a polished cloud dictation app. It uses a hotkey, supports many languages and devices, and keeps its models and clean-up in the cloud. saywhen is local-first, camera-gated and built for terminals and coding agents. It has no hotkey in the default path, shows a cancelable preview before Enter, and is free and open source. Neither one is better at everything. If you want a cloud keyboard everywhere, Wispr Flow is the more mature product. If you want your voice and camera to stay on your computer and you mostly type into a terminal or an agent, saywhen is the more honest fit. Can I try it before allowing Accessibility? Yes. The welcome screen has a practice box. Record a short phrase and saywhen shows you the raw transcript and the cleaned text inside the welcome screen. It does not type into another app, does not need Accessibility and does not save the practice to history. Allow Accessibility only when you are ready for saywhen to type into your terminal or editor. Does it work without a camera? Yes. Press Option + Space on a Mac or Alt + Space on Windows to start and stop by hand. On Home, choose Type only so Enter is never pressed until you press it. Can I make the text easier to read? Open Settings > Appearance . You can choose Light, Dark or System, turn on High contrast for black, white and amber, scale the whole window with Text size (Small, Default, Large or Extra large). The choice is remembered. Can I change the keyboard shortcut? Yes. Open Settings > Sending and click the shortcut button. Press the new combination, or press Escape to cancel. The default is Option + Space on a Mac and Alt + Space on Windows. If another app already owns the combination, saywhen keeps the old one and tells you what happened. Which apps can it type into? Any app that accepts pasted text, subject to the operating system's permissions. Enter is only pressed in apps on the trusted list in Settings. Terminals and code editors are trusted by default. Chat, email and browsers only receive typed text. Does it support languages other than English? Not yet. The current model list is English only ( tiny.en and base.en ). The app does not claim otherwise. If you need another language, do not install saywhen expecting it to work. Which Macs and Windows versions are supported? The tested build is Apple Silicon macOS. A 64-bit Windows build is produced by CI, but hands-on checks on Windows hardware are still open. An Intel Mac build is produced by CI but has not been checked on Intel hardware. The launch checklist lists exactly what has been verified and what has not. Why does my computer warn me about the installer? The beta is not signed by Apple or Microsoft yet, so Gatekeeper or SmartScreen adds an extra prompt. On a Mac, the README explains the xattr command. On Windows, click More info , then Run anyway . This warning is about the missing signature, not about the app's behaviour. Signing and notarization are required before a stable release. Where does saywhen keep my data? Settings, models and the 7-day text history live in the app data directory for your user. The exact path depends on the platform. History can be cleared from Home. There is no cloud account and no server that receives your transcripts. Can I turn off the check step? No. The preview is the safety promise. Every automatic send passes through a short, cancelable check before Enter. If you want a faster path, use Nod to send or Type only ; both keep a way out. Something is broken. What should I send? Open Problems on Home, click Copy on the message, and include: what you said and which app was in front the operating system and app version whether the camera and microphone were on the exact text from Problems Never send a recording with private content unless you choose to. Do not paste API keys or tokens into an issue. Still stuck? Read when something goes wrong , or open an issue .

title: Install saywhen with an AI assistant
text: Install saywhen with an AI assistant This file is written for an AI coding assistant (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf and similar) to follow on behalf of a person who may not be technical. If you are a person, you can follow it too: every step is a command you can copy. If this repository is already open, you are in the right place. Do not clone it again. Start at Step 1 and run every command from this folder. Rules for the assistant Ask before installing anything system-wide (Homebrew, Rust, CMake, Node.js, Visual Studio Build Tools). Say what it is, why saywhen needs it, and roughly how big it is. Explain each step in one plain sentence before running it. Avoid jargon. Say "the tool that builds the app" rather than "the Rust toolchain". Never type passwords for the person. If a step needs an admin password (for example the Homebrew installer), tell them a password prompt will appear in their terminal and wait for them. Stop and explain if a step fails. Show the last few lines of the error and suggest the next thing to try. Do not skip a failed step silently. Do not change system security settings yourself. Guide the person to click the right switches (camera, microphone, Accessibility). Step 1: Check the computer Find out the operating system and which tools already exist: uname -s; node --version; cargo --version; cmake --version; git --version On Windows (PowerShell), use: node --version; cargo --version; cmake --version; git --version saywhen needs: Tool Version Why Git any Downloads the saywhen code Node.js 20 or newer Builds the app window Rust (cargo) 1.85 or newer Builds the app engine CMake any recent Builds the speech-to-text engine Windows only: Visual Studio Build Tools with "Desktop development with C++" 2022 The C++ compiler Rust uses on Windows Step 2: Install what is missing (ask first) macOS If brew is missing, ask, then install Homebrew from brew.sh . The person will need to type their Mac password in the terminal. Then install the rest: brew install node cmake git curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y source "$HOME/.cargo/env" Xcode Command Line Tools are needed. If xcode-select -p fails, run xcode-select --install and ask the person to click Install in the popup. Windows Install, in this order, after asking: Visual Studio Build Tools 2022 from visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads with the "Desktop development with C++" workload. Node.js LTS from nodejs.org . Rust from rustup.rs (choose the default options). CMake from cmake.org/download (tick "Add CMake to the system PATH"). Git from git-scm.com . Close and reopen the terminal afterwards so the new tools are found. WebView2 is already part of Windows 10 and 11. Step 3: Get the code If INSTALL_WITH_AI.md is already in the current folder, the code is here. Stay in this folder. If it is not, download it: git clone https://github.com/ansarbuilds/saywhen.git cd saywhen Then install the app's own packages (this does not install system tools): npm ci Step 4: Start it npx tauri dev The first run downloads and verifies the camera model (about 4 MB) and prepares its runtime automatically. If this fails, check the connection and retry; do not skip asset preparation. The first build compiles everything and can take 5 to 15 minutes. Tell the person this is normal. When it finishes, the saywhen window opens, plus a small status pill near the bottom of the screen. On macOS the development build runs as saywhen-dev.app . That name is what will appear in permission prompts. Important on macOS: macOS gives camera and microphone access to the app that started saywhen. If you (the assistant) start it from your own background shell, the camera is usually blocked with "NotAllowedError". So do not start it yourself. Ask the person to open the Terminal app, then run cd saywhen && npx tauri dev there, so the permission prompts appear for them. Step 5: Walk the person through first launch Say these steps out loud, one at a time, and wait for them to confirm each one: Download a speech model: open Settings (the second item in the sidebar), find Speech model and click Download . "Tiny" (about 75 MB) is fastest. "Base" is more accurate. Allow the microphone and camera when the computer asks. macOS only, allow Accessibility: this lets saywhen type into other apps. Click Setup guide in the sidebar, then the orange badge next to Accessibility. In System Settings, turn on the switch for saywhen-dev. If there are old saywhen entries, remove them first. Pick a send style on the Home screen. Suggest Type only for the very first try, so nothing is ever sent by accident. Turn on the camera on Home, look at the screen with a closed mouth and click Calibrate . Try it: open a terminal, look at it, say "git status", and watch the text appear. Step 6: Confirm it works Ask the person: Did the status pill turn from "Waiting" to "Ready" when they looked at the screen? Did it show "Listening" when they talked? Did the words appear in the terminal? If something did not work, open the Problems list on the Home screen, read the message together, and use the table in docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md . Updating later cd saywhen && git pull && npm ci && npx tauri dev

title: When something goes wrong
text: When something goes wrong Start with the symptom. Each answer says what to check first and what to send if it still fails. Nothing gets typed Check the app in front. saywhen types into the focused app, not into a window that is behind it. On a Mac, open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility and allow saywhen , or saywhen-dev if you built it yourself. Remove old saywhen entries first if macOS shows more than one. Look at Problems on Home. If the message mentions Accessibility, click Open Accessibility settings . Try Type only on Home. If the text appears but Enter is not pressed, the problem is the app rule, not the microphone. If the target app is running as administrator on Windows, Windows blocks input from a non-elevated app. Run saywhen the same way as the target, or use the app without elevation. It never starts listening Turn the camera on. The pill should say Ready when you look at the screen. Click Calibrate while looking at the screen you actually talk to, with your mouth closed. Calibration teaches saywhen what "facing the screen" means for your desk. Check the camera preview. If it is black or frozen, see The camera sees me but it never says Ready below. Try Option + Space on a Mac or Alt + Space on Windows. If that works, the audio path is fine and the problem is the camera gate. If you use a laptop camera next to a larger monitor, turn on Camera is off to the side in Settings and calibrate while looking at the larger screen. The camera sees me but it never says Ready Make sure your face is inside the frame and the room is not backlit. A bright window behind you can hide your face. Look directly at the screen you want to talk to. Looking at a second monitor while the camera expects the first one is the most common cause. Click Calibrate again. Do not talk or smile during the 1.5 seconds. If you wear glasses, try calibrating with them on and without them. Pick the one you use most. If the app says I can see you, but you look away , the calibration is wrong for this position. Calibrate again, or turn on side-camera mode. If the camera is off to the side, the useful range is about 65 to 70 degrees of head turn. Past that, use the hotkey. It starts when I am not talking to it Turn up Settings > Noise filter . Pick Nod to send . Nothing is sent until you nod, even if it starts listening. If another person or a podcast is triggering it, the camera and microphone should both agree. Check that your lips are not in view while the other voice is speaking. Say "cancel" or press Esc during the check step. Talking again during the countdown also cancels. If it starts from a cough or a keyboard click, that is a false start. Open Problems , or use Flag False Trigger on the recent item, so the session log records it. It typed but did not press Enter The app may not be on the trusted list. Open Settings > Apps where Enter can be pressed and add it. The command may have looked risky. rm -rf , git reset --hard , git push --force and similar commands are only typed, with a warning, so you can press Enter yourself. The target app may have changed during the countdown. saywhen stops instead of pressing Enter in the wrong place. Type only mode never presses Enter. Choose Just pause , Nod to send or Say "send it" if you want automatic Enter. On a Mac, Terminal's Secure Keyboard Entry blocks synthetic input. Turn it off while using saywhen. It typed into the wrong app Check whether you switched windows during the countdown. By default, saywhen aborts when the front app changes. The default is to abort. saywhen does not yet expose a setting to paste without Enter when the app changes, so do not switch windows during the countdown if you want the text delivered. If the wrong app is consistently detected, the frontmost app detection is the thing to report. Copy the Problems message and include the app names. The model download fails or stalls Check your internet connection and try again. The download resumes from a temporary file only after the old partial file is removed, so a retry starts clean. Make sure there is enough free disk space. Tiny is about 75 MB; Base is about 142 MB. If it fails twice, try the other model. A smaller model is enough to finish setup. On a managed network, the download host may be blocked. The model comes from a pinned Hugging Face revision; ask your network administrator to allow it. Do not rename or edit files inside the models folder by hand. Download the model again from Settings instead. My microphone disappeared Unplug and replug the microphone or headset. saywhen rebuilds the audio stream and falls back to the default device. Open Settings > Microphone and pick the device again. The list refreshes when devices change. If the microphone is a Bluetooth headset, check that it is connected and not in a call that has taken exclusive control. On macOS, check System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone . On Windows, check Settings > Privacy & security > Microphone and the sound control panel. The camera stopped after I closed the window Closing the main window keeps saywhen running in the menu bar or tray. The camera gate should keep working. If the pill says Camera gate stalled , open saywhen from the tray, turn the camera off and on, and check the camera permission. On a laptop, closing the lid or locking the screen also pauses the gate until you wake it. The installer says the app is damaged or cannot be opened This beta is not signed by Apple yet. xattr -cr /Applications/saywhen.app Then open the app again. If you built the app yourself, use the saywhen-dev.app name and remove old saywhen entries from System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility before allowing the new build. On Windows, SmartScreen shows More info , then Run anyway . This is the missing signature, not a virus warning. How to send a useful report Open Problems on Home and click Copy on the message. Include: what you said, and which app was in front macOS or Windows version, a

title: How saywhen works
text: How saywhen works This page explains saywhen without any technical words. If you want the engineering detail, see ARCHITECTURE.md . The big idea Imagine talking to a friend who is helping you at your computer. You do not press a button before you speak. Your friend just knows you are talking to them, because you are looking at them and your mouth is moving. And they wait until you are finished before they act. saywhen tries to be that friend for your computer. The four helpers inside saywhen 1. The watcher (camera) The watcher looks through your webcam about 15 times a second and answers three yes-or-no questions: Is there a face? Is it looking at the screen? Are the lips moving like someone talking? It does this by finding a few hundred dots on your face (corners of your eyes, edges of your lips) and doing a little maths on them. The picture itself is thrown away straight after. Nothing is saved, nothing leaves your computer. Only the yes-or-no answers are used. What if the camera is not in front of you? Lots of people use a laptop camera next to a bigger monitor, so the camera sees the side of their face. Switch on Camera is off to the side in Settings, look at the screen you actually talk to, and click Calibrate . saywhen then treats that direction as "looking at the screen". It works until your head is turned about 65 degrees from the camera. Past that, the camera cannot see enough of your lips, so use the keyboard shortcut instead. Talking without looking (wake word). Switch on Wake word when you look away in Settings. Then, when the camera does not see you facing the screen, start your sentence with the wake word: "Eevee, run the tests". saywhen turns the first couple of seconds into text on your computer. If they do not start with "Eevee", it throws them away straight away and nothing happens. If they do, it removes "Eevee" and carries on as usual, with the check step and the countdown. A soft chime tells you it caught the wake word (one note means "go on, I am listening for the rest"). You can pick your own wake word, but a short unusual name works best: everyday words like "alright" would start by mistake. The watcher also notices two head movements: A nod means "yes, send it". A shake means "no, stop". 2. The listener (microphone) The listener checks the microphone about 30 times a second and asks: "Is this a human voice, or just noise?" It also keeps the last half second of sound in a small memory, like a tape that keeps rewinding. That way, when you start talking, your very first word is already saved, even though saywhen needed a moment to notice you. In the default hands-free mode, both the watcher and listener must agree before an utterance starts. This helps reject a podcast or another person speaking when your own lips are still. It reduces accidental starts; it does not guarantee they never happen. The manual hotkey and optional wake word provide separate ways to start. 3. The writer (speech to text) When you stop talking, the writer turns your recording into text. It uses a speech model called Whisper that runs on your own computer (on a Mac it uses the graphics chip). In the recorded Apple Silicon benchmark, 1.5 seconds of audio took 87 to 473 milliseconds to transcribe with Tiny.en. Your model and hardware will affect the time. Then a tidy-up step fixes the words developers use a lot: You say It writes "cargo test dash dash release" cargo test --release "cubectal get pods" kubectl get pods "um, git status" git status You can teach it your own words too (project names, tools) in Settings. 4. The sender (typing it for you) The sender shows you the text for a moment, then types it into the app you are using, and presses Enter if it is allowed to. How it decides to send depends on the send style you picked: Send style When it sends Just pause After a short countdown (about 2 seconds) Nod to send Only when you nod. If you do not nod in 15 seconds, nothing is sent. Say "send it" Only presses Enter if your sentence ended with "send it" Type only Never presses Enter, only types And you can always stop it: shake your head, press Esc, or (in the countdown) just start talking again. The manual shortcut can be changed in Settings > Sending ; the default is Option + Space on a Mac and Alt + Space on Windows. The five moods of saywhen Concept animation with simplified timing. Static alternative . You can see which mood saywhen is in by the colour of the window and the small floating pill. The colours below are the defaults, taken from the saywhen logo (plum, silver and amber). In Settings > Appearance you can choose System, Light or Dark, pick another palette, and choose whether the glow changes with each mood. There is also a Guide page inside the app with the do's and don'ts. Mood What it means Colour Waiting Nobody is looking at the screen Calm plum Ready You are looking. Start talking any time. A soft silver glow Listening You are talking and it is recording Amber, the bars move with your voice Writing It is turning your voice into text Lilac, with a spinning ring Check It is showing you the text before sending Amber countdown bar The safety rules saywhen is careful about pressing Enter, because Enter makes things happen. Only in safe apps. It presses Enter in terminals and code editors you trust. In chat apps, email and web browsers it only types, so a half-finished message is never sent to a person. Never risky commands. If the text looks dangerous (deleting files with rm -rf , git push --force and similar), it only types it and shows a warning. You press Enter yourself if you really mean it. Never the wrong window. If you switch to a different app while it is counting down, it stops instead of typing into the wrong place. Always a way out. Every send can be cancelled. And there is always a keyboard shortcut (Option + Space on Mac, Alt + Space on Windows) if you do not want to use the camera at all. What is kept, and what is not Thing Kept? Camera pictures Never. Thrown away

title: Changelog
text: Changelog Unreleased The onboarding window keeps Start talking visible at the default window size, traps focus, closes with Escape and restores focus when it closes. The onboarding microphone and camera badges now reflect the device list and the camera state instead of being hard-coded. Model downloads show a real progress bar and percentage in Settings and on the setup checklist. The "Say something" setup step is only marked done after text is successfully injected. The check step scrolls into view when it appears, so it is visible at the minimum window size. The check step can no longer be turned off. Every automatic send goes through a cancelable review. Send-style cards support arrow-key navigation. Renamed Lab to Diagnostics and moved the practice box and live numbers under that name. Removed the marketing demo button from Home and hid the Problems panel until there is a real problem. The HUD now appears on the display under the pointer, and the tray has a "Move HUD to This Display" action. It stays click-through on purpose so it can never steal focus; send and cancel remain on the keyboard and in the main window. Added a searchable static docs hub in docs-site/ (build with npm run docs:build ). Added a command palette on Cmd+K / Ctrl+K for navigation, listening, camera, theme, contrast, text size and help actions. Added a skippable first-run intro, with a Replay the intro command. Added high contrast mode, an in-app reduce-motion switch and four text-size steps that scale the window through the webview. The dark theme now uses brighter text, stronger surfaces and contrast-checked labels; sent, cancel and error actions have short motion cues. The push-to-talk shortcut can be recorded and reset in Settings > Sending. The HUD and the in-app Guide follow the new binding. If the combination is already taken, the old shortcut is restored and the error is shown. Onboarding now has a Try it now practice box: record a short command and see the raw and cleaned text without typing into another app or needing Accessibility. Recent has a Paste last button, and Cmd+Ctrl+V on Mac or Ctrl+Alt+V on Windows types the last transcript again without pressing Enter. Settings now has a section navigation bar, a search field, an app picker for the trusted-apps list, and an About section with a privacy-safe diagnostics copy. Added a System, Light or Dark theme. The choice is remembered and follows the system when set to System. Moved the custom vocabulary into its own Words section and renamed Colours to Appearance. Added a user FAQ and expanded troubleshooting for permissions, camera stalls, microphone loss, secure input, elevation and model downloads. Fixed the broken #see-it-work link in the documentation index. v0.2.0 beta First public beta for Apple Silicon macOS and 64-bit Windows. Local Whisper transcription, camera-gated hands-free listening, pre-roll, preview, send styles, 7-day history and the in-app Guide. Developer cleanup for CLI commands, custom vocabulary, "scratch that", "paste only", and a destructive-command guard.

title: Architecture
text: Architecture Status: implemented beta. Hardware validation gaps and release gates are tracked in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md . Measurements below describe the specific recorded sessions, not a guarantee for other hardware. Stack Shell: Tauri v2 (Rust backend, TypeScript frontend in the system webview). Vision: MediaPipe Tasks Vision (Face Landmarker) running in the webview via WASM/WebGL. Chosen because it works the same on macOS, Windows and Linux without native per-platform vision code. Audio capture: cpal in Rust ( src-tauri/src/audio.rs ) with automatic hot-plug recovery ( evaluate_audio_stream_health ), preferred-device restoration, and wall-clock system sleep/lock detection ( detect_system_sleep_or_stall_jump ). Voice activity detection: Silero VAD (ONNX). Transcription: whisper.cpp (via Rust bindings), with Tiny.en and Base.en available. Models downloaded on first run to <app_data_dir>/models in packaged .app / .exe builds (or ./models in dev runs), never committed. AI cleanup: deterministic local developer pass ( src-tauri/src/cleanup.rs , < 50 us ) plus opt-in secondary local Ollama ( http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions ) or OpenAI-compatible BYOK pass ( run_opt_in_llm_cleanup , off by default, 1.2s timeout with deterministic fallback). Text injection: enigo for keystrokes ( src-tauri/src/inject.rs , inject/macos.rs , inject/windows.rs ), clipboard paste via arboard as the default path, then a synthetic Enter after a length-scaled delay. Storage: <app_data_dir>/utterance-history.jsonl for 7-day local transcript history ( src-tauri/src/history.rs ), automatically pruned on startup and write ( HISTORY_RETENTION_MS = 7 days , MAX_HISTORY_ENTRIES = 200 ), with one-click purge. Settings in <app_data_dir>/settings.local.json (a legacy repo-root settings.local.json is copied there once on first launch). Pipeline flowchart TD Camera["Webcam frames in memory"] --> Vision["MediaPipe face features"] Mic["Microphone audio"] --> VAD["Pre-roll and Silero VAD"] Vision --> Gate{"Intent gate"} VAD --> Gate Gate --> Speech["Capture and local Whisper"] Speech --> Cleanup["Developer cleanup"] Cleanup --> Preview["Cancelable preview"] Preview --> Policy{"Target and send rules"} Policy --> Paste["Paste only"] Policy --> Enter["Paste and Enter"] Preview --> Cancel["Cancel"] The webview sends only derived numbers (landmark-based features such as MAR, yaw, pitch, face present, gesture events) to Rust over Tauri IPC. Raw frames never leave the webview process memory. Windows and background run main window: settings, webcam preview and the vision loop. Closing it hides it; the app keeps running (tray menu or macOS Dock reopen brings it back). The vision loop is ticked by a dedicated Worker timer so it keeps running when the window is hidden, and skips DOM work while hidden. hud window: transparent, always-on-top, non-focusable and click-through ( set_ignore_cursor_events(true) ). It only listens to backend events ( audio-telemetry , preview-started , utterance-complete , ...) and never takes focus, so the frontmost app stays the injection target. Because the HUD cannot be clicked, src-tauri/src/hud.rs registers a global Esc shortcut only while the pipeline is in PREVIEW and unregisters it right after, so saywhen never swallows Esc outside the countdown. The backend tracks whether the camera gate is switched on ( set_camera_gate_enabled ). Telemetry carries cameraEnabled and visionActive , and the HUD shows a stall warning when the gate is on but frames stopped arriving. Reliable text injection and safety guards Native frontmost app detection ( FrontmostApp { name, bundle_id, exe, pid, detection_us } ): macOS ( src-tauri/src/inject/macos.rs ): queries NSWorkspace.sharedWorkspace.frontmostApplication via objc2-app-kit inside an autorelease pool ( 1 us to 2 us warm median latency over 20 calls, down from 8,336 us with two /usr/bin/lsappinfo subprocesses). Windows ( src-tauri/src/inject/windows.rs ): queries GetForegroundWindow + GetWindowThreadProcessId + QueryFullProcessImageNameW via windows-sys without spawning PowerShell. Linux ( src-tauri/src/inject/linux.rs ): queries X11 _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW -> _NET_WM_PID / WM_CLASS / _NET_WM_NAME + /proc/<pid>/exe , and fails loudly with clipboard fallback if running under pure Wayland without XWayland DISPLAY . Exact allowlist and self-injection guard: Matches exact app names (case-insensitive), macOS bundle identifiers (such as com.apple.Terminal , com.googlecode.iterm2 , dev.warp.Warp-Stable , com.mitchellh.ghostty , com.microsoft.VSCode , com.todesktop.230313mzl4w4u92 , dev.zed.Zed , com.anthropic.claudefordesktop ), and Windows executable names ( WindowsTerminal.exe , Code.exe , Cursor.exe , etc.). Substring matches (such as "Xcode" matching "Code" ) are rejected. saywhen itself ( dev.saywhen.app , saywhen.exe , or matching PID) is removed from the default allowlist and unconditionally refused so saywhen never types into or presses Enter on its own windows. Pre-injection target verification ( onTargetChanged: "abort" | "paste_only" , default "abort" ): Right before injecting at the end of the preview countdown, saywhen re-detects the frontmost app and compares PID, bundle ID, executable, and name against the preview target. If the user switched apps during the countdown, saywhen never presses Enter: it either aborts (leaving the transcript on the clipboard and surfacing an error) or pastes without Enter ( "paste_only" ). Multi-monitor gaze-window alignment guard ( evaluate_gaze_window_alignment in src-tauri/src/inject/policy.rs ): Compares the focused target window's horizontal display coordinates ( window_center_x , primary_screen_width ) against the user's calibrated head yaw ( head_yaw_deg ). If the focused window is on an external left display while the user is looking right, or on an external right display while the user is looking left, saywhen downgrades delivery to Paste-Only ( will_press_enter = false ) so it never auto-fires Enter into a terminal on the

title: How we built saywhen
text: How we built saywhen This is the story of saywhen, told simply. Measurements below come from specific prototype sessions and synthetic replay tests, not a broad user study. The full technical log lives in ROADMAP.md . The itch Talking to a coding assistant should feel like talking to a colleague. But every voice tool had the same two annoyances: You had to press a key to start. Your hands had to come back to the keyboard just to talk, which misses the point of using your voice. You had to press Enter at the end. The tool typed your words and then waited. For a short command, that last key press is most of the work. And tools that listened all the time without a key started recording every podcast, phone call and chat in the room. The idea: use the webcam as a second pair of ears. If you are looking at the screen and your lips are moving while the microphone hears a voice, you are almost certainly talking to the computer. Stage 1: Can a webcam even tell? (1 November 2026) Before building an app, we built a tiny test page to answer one question: can a normal laptop webcam tell, reliably and quickly, whether someone is facing the screen and talking? We used Google's free MediaPipe face tracker, which finds about 470 points on a face. From those points we worked out the head angle and how open the mouth is. What we learned: It is fast : 12 to 15 milliseconds per frame, in the prototype sessions. That does not yet establish whole-app CPU or battery cost. "Facing the screen or not" was separated 100% of the time in our test sessions. "Mouth still" was correctly ignored 96.2% of the time. But the camera alone cannot tell chewing or smiling from talking. That proved we needed the microphone too. Neither sensor is enough on its own; together they are. Stage 2: A plain voice typer (2 November 2026) Next we built the boring but essential part: a desktop app (Tauri, with a Rust engine) that records your voice, turns it into text with Whisper on your own computer, and types it into your terminal when you press a hotkey. Two important tricks went in here: A half-second rewind buffer. The microphone always keeps the last 0.5 seconds of sound, so the first word is never lost while the app decides you are talking. Whisper on the graphics chip. On an Apple Silicon Mac, 1.5 seconds of speech turns into text in 87 to 473 milliseconds. Stage 3: No more hotkey (2 November 2026) Then we joined the camera and the microphone together. saywhen got its five moods: Waiting, Ready, Listening, Writing, Check. It starts listening only when your face, your lips and your voice all agree, and it stops when you go quiet. A nod finishes early, a head shake cancels. Stage 4: Tidy words and safe sending (2 November 2026) Speech-to-text is bad at developer words. "cargo test dash dash release" is not what you want in a terminal. We wrote a clean-up step that turns spoken commands into real ones, and taught it the common mistakes Whisper makes ("cubectal" means kubectl ). We also made sending safe: A countdown before every send, so you can read and cancel. Enter is only pressed in trusted apps (terminals, editors). Chat apps and email only get typed text. Risky commands like rm -rf are never sent automatically. Stage 5: Windows and a first welcome screen (2 November 2026) saywhen learned to run on Windows, got a welcome screen explaining permissions, and remembered your settings between launches. Making it really good (3 and 4 November 2026) With the basics working, we spent two days on the hard details. A few highlights: Starting and stopping at the right moment. We built 56 test clips (computer-generated speech with simulated camera traces, so not live users yet) and replayed them through the old and new logic. Starting by mistake went from 36.4% to 0% , and cutting people off mid-sentence went from 52.9% to 0% . Developer words. On 34 spoken commands, exact matches went from 44.1% to 100% . Typing reliably. saywhen checks which app is in front before it pastes, waits a little longer for long text, puts your clipboard back afterwards, and refuses to type into the wrong window. Finding the front app on macOS went from about 8 milliseconds to about 0.002. Real life. Unplugging headphones, closing the laptop lid and locking the screen are all handled without sending anything by accident. Spoken fixes. "scratch that", "paste only" and "never mind" work while you talk. History. The last 7 days of what you said, searchable, on your computer only. Choosing how you send, and a new look (8 November 2026) People asked for different ways to send. Some love nodding, some never want Enter pressed for them. So saywhen now has four send styles you pick with one click: Just pause, Nod to send, Say "send it", and Type only. You can also cancel a countdown just by talking again (saying "cancel" or "wait"). At the same time the app got a complete makeover. It now uses a warm, magazine-like design with bundled fonts that work offline, and the window gently changes colour with each mood so you can tell what saywhen is doing from across the room. Cameras off to the side (8 November 2026) The first tester to try the new look had a laptop camera beside a big monitor, so the camera saw the side of their face. saywhen said "looking away" and "lips still" even while they were talking. Three fixes: calibration can now point up to 65 degrees away from the camera (it stopped at 45), a Camera is off to the side switch widens the allowed head turn, and the lip measurement now corrects for how a turned head makes the mouth look narrower. A logo and a calmer look (8 November 2026) saywhen got its own logo: a ribbon "S" in silver and amber on deep plum. The app was redesigned around it, aiming for the calm, rounded feel of the best voice tools: soft white cards, rounded buttons, one strong colour (plum) and amber only for "live" moments like listening and the send countdown. The logo now sits in the sidebar, the welcome screen, the floating pill and the app i

title: What has been measured
text: What has been measured These numbers come from prototype sessions on an Apple Silicon Mac. The films and animations in this repository are illustrations, and their timing is not a measurement. The numbers below are. Part What we measured Result Face tracking (MediaPipe) Time per camera frame 12 to 15 ms "Facing the screen" check Telling facing from turned away 100% on our test sessions "Mouth still" check Ignoring a closed or still mouth 96.2% rejected correctly Start and end of speech 56 test clips (generated speech plus simulated camera traces, not live users) 0% false starts (was 36.4%), 0% cut-offs (was 52.9%) Developer word clean-up 34 spoken commands 34 of 34 exact (was 44.1%) Speech to text (Whisper tiny.en, GPU) 1.5 s of audio 87 to 473 ms Finding the front app (macOS) Median of 20 calls 1 to 2 microseconds The start-and-end-of-speech clips are generated speech with simulated camera traces, not live users. Real-user accuracy, CPU and battery use are not measured yet. The launch checklist lists what has been checked on which hardware. Run the replay benchmark yourself: cargo run --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --bin replay -- recordings

title: Risks
text: Risks Risk Why it matters Mitigation Unreliable lip signal Glasses, beards, masks, bad lighting, side angles or low-res webcams may make MAR noisy. The whole idea depends on it. Stage 1 spike with real-desk tests and a hard 90% separation exit. Combine multiple features. Per-user calibration. Kill or pivot the idea if it fails. Auto-Enter sends the wrong thing A misheard shell command could do real damage. Cancelable preview with countdown. Per-app rules (paste-only by default for risky apps). Never auto-send in apps not on the allow list. Optional confirm for destructive-looking commands. Always-on camera trust Users are rightly wary of an app that watches them. Frames in memory only, never saved or sent. Visible indicator, one-click pause. Open source code. Clear privacy doc. Webview throttling A hidden webview may throttle camera, timers or WebGL, killing the visual gate. Test in Stage 1. Mitigated (unverified on hardware): Worker-timer vision loop, backgroundThrottling: disabled on macOS 14+, WebView2 anti-throttling args and Web Lock on Windows. The HUD pill flags a stalled gate. Remaining fallbacks: move vision into the always-visible HUD window, or native vision fast path. CPU and battery Continuous vision at 10 to 15 FPS could drain laptops. Measure early. Adaptive frame rate (low FPS in IDLE, higher in ARMED). Pause on battery saver or when the screen locks. Linux / Wayland Wayland restricts global input injection and window focus info. Defer Linux to Stage 6. X11 first. Investigate portals and ydotool-style approaches later. Crowded market Many free offline dictation apps already exist. Position narrowly: hands-free voice for coding agents and terminals. Compete on no-hotkey intent and safe auto-submit, not on transcription. Scope creep Gestures, gaze targeting, cleanup tuning and multi-platform could swallow the project. Strict staged roadmap with exit criteria. Park ideas in IDEA_LOG.md. Accessibility and fairness Lip-movement detection may work worse for some faces, speech patterns, disabilities or cultural differences. A manual hotkey fallback is always available. Test with varied people before going public. Make thresholds tunable and calibration easy.

title: Roadmap
text: Roadmap Launch readiness follow-up The launch hardening pass adds verified camera-asset preparation, staged speech-model downloads, release version/tag checks and automated tests before packaging. The macOS debug bundle builds locally. Public launch gates, platform testing and signing remain pending in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md . Historical implementation completion below does not imply those gates have passed. Each stage has an exit criterion. Do not start the next stage until the current one passes, or the reason for skipping is written down. Stage 0: Prior-art search Status: Skipped on 2026-11-01 (User directed focus directly to prototype feasibility and open-source implementation). Work through the checklist in PRIOR_ART.md . Exit: a written summary of who has built webcam-gated or lip-triggered voice input, how it worked, and what is left that is worth building. Stage 1: Feasibility spike Status: Completed on 2026-11-01 (Spike built in spikes/stage1-mediapipe/ ). Minimal page running MediaPipe Face Landmarker, plotting MAR and head yaw live. Test at the real desk: with and without glasses, different lighting (day, night, backlit), different camera angles and distances. Record labeled sessions: talking, silent, yawning, chewing, smiling, turned away. Test whether a hidden Tauri webview keeps the camera and WebGL running. Measure CPU at 10 to 15 FPS. Empirical Measurements (VERIFIED): Gaze Gate ( |yaw| <= 22° , |pitch| <= 20° ): 100.0% separation. Silence Gate: 96.2% rejection. Inference Latency: 12 ms to 15 ms per frame (over 65 FPS capable, runs easily capped at 15 FPS with negligible CPU). Yawn Ceiling ( MAR <= 0.45 ): Filters anatomical wide-mouth stretches. Key finding: Vision alone cannot separate chewing or smiling from speech without audio; conclusively proves the necessity of multimodal microphone VAD fusion in Stage 2. Exit: Feasibility confirmed. Multimodal necessity validated for Stage 2. Stage 2: Handy-core dictation Status: Completed on 2026-11-02 (Tauri v2 + Rust audio core in src-tauri/ ). Rebuild the basics, studying Handy for patterns: cpal capture, Silero VAD, whisper.cpp / Parakeet, text injection, manual hotkey. Empirical Measurements (VERIFIED): Audio Pipeline: 16 kHz mono resampling with 500 ms ( 8,000 samples) circular pre-roll ring buffer and 32 ms ( 512 samples) Silero VAD v5 ONNX chunks. Whisper Metal Inference ( ggml-tiny.en.bin ): 473 ms on a 1,500 ms utterance ( 0.315x Real-Time Factor) on Apple Silicon GPU. Text Injection: Main-thread enigo controller with clipboard paste ( Cmd+V ) and global Option + Space hotkey. Exit: Reliable hotkey dictation into a terminal on macOS. Stage 3: Gated auto start/stop Status: Built and active on 2026-11-02 (Multimodal vision + audio state machine wired in src/ and src-tauri/ ). Wire the visual gate into the state machine (IDLE > ARMED > LISTENING > TRANSCRIBING). Ring buffer so the first syllable is not clipped. Head gestures ( nod = transcribe now, shake = cancel) and end phrase stripping ( "send it" ). Live false-trigger and missed-start session telemetry tracker in UI. Exit: start and stop work hands-free with a measured false-trigger rate and missed-start rate over a normal work session. Stage 4: Cleanup, preview, auto-Enter Status: Built and active on 2026-11-02 ( src-tauri/src/cleanup.rs , src-tauri/src/inject.rs , src/main.ts ). AI cleanup pass (local deterministic developer rules or opt-in BYOK) that keeps code identifiers, paths ( slash , dot rs , dot ts ) and CLI flags ( dash dash release -> --release ) intact while stripping filler words. Cancelable preview HUD with live countdown ( 1.8s default), instant Esc / head-shake cancel, and Enter / head-nod confirm. Auto-Enter with per-app rules ( lsappinfo frontmost app detection: auto-send in terminals and coding agents, paste-only in chat apps and email, plus destructive command guard for rm -rf , git reset --hard , etc.). Exit: a full day of real use with zero unwanted sends. Stage 5: Windows, polish, go public Status: Completed on 2026-11-02 ( src-tauri/src/inject.rs , src-tauri/src/audio.rs , index.html , README.md , docs/screenshots/ ). Windows support (WebView2, PowerShell Win32 GetForegroundWindow detection, Ctrl+V clipboard injection). Onboarding modal with privacy & permissions checklist, camera permission UX, and persistent settings.local.json configuration. Automated headless Chrome screenshot pipeline ( scripts/capture-screenshots.sh ) capturing Stages 1 to 5 in docs/screenshots/ . Exit: documented, cross-platform ready, and pushed to GitHub. Post-Stage 5: Floating HUD pill and background vision Status: Implemented on 2026-11-03. Compiles and unit tests pass on Linux. Manually checked on macOS on 2026-11-04 (pill visible, injection lands in Terminal, global Esc cancel, close-to-background with camera gate, tray menu). Not yet measured: 10+ minute hidden-window vision run. Not yet tested on Windows. Transparent, always-on-top, non-focusable, click-through hud window ( hud.html , src/hud.ts , src-tauri/src/hud.rs ) placed bottom-center of the primary work area. Shows state, mic level, listening timer, preview text with countdown, injection result, and a loud warning when the camera gate is on but vision frames stopped. Global Esc registered only while in PREVIEW , so the click-through HUD is still cancelable without stealing focus from the target app. Closing the main window hides it; saywhen keeps running with the HUD and camera gate. Tray menu: open, pause/resume camera gate, show/hide HUD, cancel, quit. macOS Dock reopen shows the window. Without a tray (and outside macOS) closing quits. Vision loop driven by a Worker timer instead of requestAnimationFrame , backgroundThrottling: disabled (macOS 14+), WebView2 anti-throttling browser args and a held Web Lock (Windows). DOM and canvas work is skipped while hidden. whisper-rs metal feature now only enabled on macOS targets, which unblocks Windows and Linux builds. Screenshot of all HUD states: docs/screenshot

title: Prior art
text: Prior art Status: the Stage 0 search has NOT been done. This page lists what is known so far, and what still needs to be checked. Nothing here supports a claim that saywhen is novel. Known tools in the space These are mostly offline or local dictation apps. Details below are from memory and need verifying in Stage 0. Tool Notes (to verify) Handy (cjpais/Handy) Tauri v2 + Rust, Whisper and Parakeet, Silero VAD, MIT, around 35k stars. Strong proof of demand for free offline dictation. Hotkey driven. Main code reference for Stage 2. Pindrop Local macOS dictation app (WhisperKit). Discontinued and replaced by Sayso (justsayso.app). Yap Local dictation app. VoiceInk Local dictation app for macOS. Whispur Local dictation app. TypeNo Local dictation app. miniwhisper Small Whisper-based dictation tool. FluidVoice Local dictation app. OpenWhispr Open source Whisper dictation app. Voicetypr Local dictation app. Earshot (Leonxlnx/earshot) "Ears for coding agents", around 3.4k stars. Close to our positioning, check in Stage 0. For each, record: platforms, trigger method (hotkey, wake word, always-on), whether it auto-submits, cleanup approach, license, activity. Stage 0 search checklist Visual VAD : research and code on visual voice activity detection (detecting speech from video of the face). Webcam lip-triggered dictation : any app or project that starts dictation when lips move on camera. Look-to-talk : gaze or attention-based activation (for example, assistants that activate when you look at the device). MediaPipe mouth-open speech detection : demos, blog posts or repos using MediaPipe face landmarks to detect speaking. Talon Voice and OS voice control overlap : what Talon, macOS Voice Control and Windows Voice Access already do for hands-free input, and whether any use the camera (for example eye tracking or face gestures). Patents on camera-gated speech recognition or lip-movement-triggered input. Each tool in the table above checked for any camera or no-hotkey mode. Output: a short summary in this file with links, what each does, and what gap remains.

title: Idea log
text: Idea log How this idea was chosen Asked Gemini for 50 project ideas. The list was generic and not useful. Asked Gemini again for a list tailored to my existing repos. That list was much better. Looked closely at Handy (cjpais/Handy). It proved there is real demand for free, offline dictation, but that space is now crowded with clones (Pindrop, VoiceInk, Yap, Whispur, TypeNo and others). Noticed the open slot: no-hotkey multimodal intent sensing (face + gaze + lips + speech) combined with safe auto-submit, aimed at coding agents and terminals. Decided on this idea. Stack decision: Tauri + MediaPipe, so the same vision code runs cross-platform in the webview. Parked ideas Not dead, just not now. QuickLook extension for parquet, duckdb and sqlite files. Chrome MV3 animation inspector. csv-autopsy webhook-bench blender-checkpoint calibrate-llm SceneBoardKit Naming The first working name was dropped because it suggests lip-reading (a non-goal), makes the camera feel more invasive, and ties the brand to one signal. Considered and rejected: Sayso (taken by the Pindrop rebrand, a direct competitor), Earshot (existing "ears for coding agents" repo), nokey (reads as "no API key" or a password tool, and a manual hotkey fallback exists anyway), Heed, Utter, Hark (taken everywhere). Picked saywhen (2026-11-01): "say when" is the everyday phrase for "tell me when you are done", which is the auto-stop and auto-send idea. Backup was saydo.

title: Vision
text: Vision The problem Talking to a coding agent or a terminal should be as easy as talking to a colleague sitting next to you. Today it is not. Hotkey friction. Every dictation tool wants you to press and hold (or toggle) a key. Your hands have to come back to the keyboard just to start talking, which defeats the point of voice. Review-then-send friction. Most tools paste the text and stop. You read it, then reach for Enter. For short agent prompts and shell commands, that second step is most of the effort. Audio-only VAD misfires. Voice activity detection on audio alone cannot tell the difference between you talking to the computer, you talking to someone in the room, a podcast, or a call. So tools either need a hotkey or they trigger on everything. The idea Use the webcam as a second sensor for intent. If you are in front of the screen, facing it, your lips are moving and the mic hears speech, you are very likely talking to the computer. Combine those signals and you can skip the hotkey entirely. Trigger (start listening) All of these must hold at the same time: Face present in the camera frame. Facing the screen : head yaw and pitch within a calibrated range. Lips moving : mouth aspect ratio (MAR) shows variance over a sliding window of about 300ms. A static open mouth (yawn) or slow rhythmic motion (chewing) should not count. Speech : audio VAD (Silero) reports speech in the same window. Audio is buffered in a short ring buffer, so the first syllable is not lost while the visual gate decides. Stop (end of utterance) Any of: Silence and closed mouth for about 500 to 800ms (tunable). End phrase , for example "send it", which is stripped from the final text. Gesture : nod = send now, head shake = cancel. User flow saywhen runs in the background. A small indicator shows the current state. You look at your terminal or agent and start talking. The indicator switches to "listening". You stop talking. Audio is transcribed locally. The AI cleanup pass tidies the text (filler words, punctuation, code identifiers kept intact). A short preview appears near the cursor with a countdown. You can cancel by shaking your head, saying "cancel", pressing Esc, or looking away. If not canceled, the text is typed into the focused app and Enter is pressed. The 7-second demo GIF The demo that sells it, with no narration needed: Hands visibly off the keyboard. The user looks at a terminal running Claude Code and says: "run the tests and fix any failures". The preview pops up with the cleaned text. The user nods. The prompt is submitted and the agent starts running the tests. Seven seconds, zero keys pressed.

title: Contributing to saywhen
text: Contributing to saywhen Thanks for wanting to help. Bug reports, tuning data and small fixes are all welcome. Before you start For anything bigger than a small fix, open an issue first so we can agree on the approach. Read AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md . The principles there are not optional: local-first, private, always cancelable, fail loudly, measure everything. Set up You need Node.js 20 or newer, Rust and CMake (see the README). The Rust version is pinned in rust-toolchain.toml , and rustup installs it for you. Please be kind and patient with each other: see the Code of Conduct . npm install npx tauri dev Before you open a pull request npm run build cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml If you changed when saywhen starts or stops listening, also run the replay benchmark and paste the before and after numbers into the pull request: cargo run --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --bin replay -- --generate-corpus recordings Rules of the road Privacy first. Never write camera frames to disk, send them anywhere or log them. Audio is only kept when the user opts in. Never commit model files ( *.bin , *.gguf , *.onnx ), recordings or settings.local.json . Numbers, not vibes. Claims about accuracy, speed, CPU or battery need a measurement. Say what you verified and what you assumed. No em dashes in docs or code comments. CI checks this. Plain language in anything a user reads. Keep pull requests small and focused on one thing. Reporting a bug Use the bug report template. The Problems panel on the Home screen has a copy button for the error message. Please do not attach recordings of your voice or screenshots that show private text.

title: Security and privacy
text: Security and privacy saywhen uses your camera and microphone and types into other apps, so we take security and privacy reports seriously. Reporting a problem Please do not open a public issue for a security or privacy problem. Use GitHub's private reporting instead: go to the Security tab of this repository and click Report a vulnerability . You should hear back within a week. What counts Camera frames or audio being saved, logged or sent anywhere without the user opting in. Text being typed or Enter being pressed in an app the user did not expect. A way around the risky command guard or the trusted app list. Anything that lets another app or website control saywhen. Supported versions Only the latest release gets fixes.

title: Code of Conduct
text: Code of Conduct saywhen follows the Contributor Covenant, version 2.1 . In short: Be kind and patient. People here have different backgrounds and different levels of experience. Talk about the work, not the person. No harassment, insults or unwelcome personal attention, in issues, pull requests or anywhere else connected to the project. Reporting If someone's behavior is a problem, contact the maintainer privately through the contact details on the maintainer's GitHub profile . Reports are kept confidential. The maintainer may edit or remove comments, and may block people who keep breaking these rules. Security and privacy problems go through SECURITY.md instead.

title: Launch checklist
text: Launch checklist Status: beta preparation complete locally; public launch sign-off is pending. Gate Apple Silicon Intel Mac Windows x64 Clean checkout: npm ci , npm test , npm run check:release , npm run build Local pass on 2026-11-12 (macOS 27.0.1, M4, existing checkout); CI pending Pending CI Pending CI Locked Rust tests pass Local pass on 2026-11-12 (46 passed, 3 ignored) Pending Pending Release installer builds and opens on a fresh account Pending Pending Pending Camera, microphone and typing permissions: deny, retry, grant Pending Pending Pending Download Tiny, interrupt the download, retry, restart Pending Pending Pending Disconnect internet after setup: camera and dictation work Pending Pending Pending Type only, pause, nod and phrase modes behave as labeled Pending Pending Pending Esc, shake and speech cancel before injection Pending Pending Pending Switch app during preview: no delivery to the new app Pending Pending Pending Switch app after paste: no Enter in the new app Pending Pending Pending Risky commands are downgraded; no unintended execution Pending Pending Pending Hide window for 10 minutes: gate remains active Pending Pending Pending Sleep/wake, mic unplug/reconnect: no stale send Pending Pending Pending Full work session: record unwanted sends and missed starts Pending Pending Pending Signing and installer security prompts documented Pending Pending Pending Use a disposable terminal with harmless commands for delivery tests. The destructive-command matcher is a heuristic, not a shell parser or a guarantee against dangerous commands. Test risky strings in an editor, never a live shell. Paste itself can execute multiline input in some terminals. Run hardware-dependent tests explicitly from an interactive desktop, after downloading Tiny: cargo test --locked --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml -- --ignored --test-threads=1 The GPU benchmark crashed inside Metal allocation in the restricted agent session. It remains a required hardware check; excluding it from unattended unit tests is not a fix or proof of runtime compatibility. The clipboard test temporarily replaces clipboard contents, so run it when the clipboard can be used for testing. Prepare the release Complete the gates for every platform being advertised. Omit unverified platform installers from a public release, or label them explicitly experimental. Choose an unused version and update package.json , package-lock.json , src-tauri/Cargo.toml , src-tauri/Cargo.lock and src-tauri/tauri.conf.json together. Run npm run check:release . Configure the Apple signing and notarization secrets listed in .github/workflows/release.yml . Verify the final downloaded app with codesign --verify --deep --strict and spctl --assess --type execute . Windows signing still needs separate configuration or a clearly disclosed unsigned beta. Push reviewed changes and a matching v<version> tag. The workflow creates a draft prerelease , not a public release. All intended matrix jobs must pass; a successful platform alone is not enough. Download and test the actual installers. Add release notes with supported OS/hardware, signing status, first-run instructions, known limitations and the exact test evidence. Check the README demo links and attach the referenced video assets. The README clip links to the project page at https://ansarbuilds.dev/p/saywhen/ , so that page must be live before the repository goes public. Publish the draft only after the gates pass. Mark it stable only after the hardware evidence supports that claim. Remaining hardening Speech downloads use HTTPS, bounded retries, a temporary file and GGML format/size sanity checks. Since 2026-11-12 they are also pinned to one revision of the model repository and to SHA-256 digests. Both digests were checked against real downloads of Tiny and Base. The v0.2.0 installers predate this, so it ships with the next build. A restrictive webview CSP is set in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json . Before merging, run npx tauri dev and a release build, then confirm: the window and HUD draw with their fonts, the camera turns on and Calibrate works, a phrase is transcribed and typed, and the webview console shows no "Content Security Policy" errors. Review optional remote cleanup and API-key storage before advertising it for sensitive work. Real-user accuracy, CPU and battery results are still needed. Existing replay numbers are synthetic-corpus results.

Look at the screen. Say the command. saywhen types it, and can press Enter. No hotkey. The camera picture is never saved. Speech stays on your computer. You see the words before they go anywhere. [ONE_USE] Beta for Mac and Windows. Not signed yet. https://github.com/ansarbuilds/saywhen A longer post, for LinkedIn or a blog intro: I made saywhen, a free desktop app for talking to the terminal or coding agent in front of you. You look at the screen and talk. The camera checks that a face is there, facing the screen, with lips moving. The microphone checks for speech. Those have to agree before it listens, so there is no key to hold. The words are written on your computer. A short preview appears. Esc, a head shake, or talking again throws them away. If you let it go, saywhen types them and can press Enter. [ONE_USE] It is a beta for Mac and Windows. This build is not signed by Apple or Microsoft yet. After the speech model is downloaded, it works offline. The picture from the camera is never saved. https://ansarbuilds.dev/p/saywhen/ Show HN Title: Show HN: saywhen – look at the screen and say the command Body: saywhen is a free, open-source desktop app for Mac and Windows. You look at the screen and talk. It types the command into the focused app and can press Enter. You can stop it. I built it because dictation tools made me hold a key, and then press Enter after I had already said the thing. For a short prompt to a coding agent, that was most of the work. How it starts: a face is in frame, the head is turned toward the screen, the lips are moving, and the microphone hears speech. All four have to be true. The camera picture stays in memory for a moment and is thrown away. Speech is transcribed on the machine with Whisper. A preview shows the cleaned text. Esc, a head shake, or speaking again cancels it. [ONE_USE] What is honest about this beta: - [MAC_STATUS] on Mac, [WINDOWS_STATUS] on Windows. macOS may say the app is damaged until you clear the quarantine flag. Windows SmartScreen asks an extra question. The README has the one step. You can also build it from the repo. - Enter is pressed only in apps you mark as trusted. Risky commands such as rm -rf are typed with a warning. You press Enter yourself. That check is a heuristic, not a guarantee. - If you switch apps during the preview, it does not type into the new app. - The turn-taking numbers in the README are from generated clips and simulated camera traces, not from a study of live users. - Real-device checks for a signed Mac build, Intel Macs, and Windows are still open: https://github.com/ansarbuilds/saywhen/blob/main/docs/LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md Try Type only first, so Enter is never pressed. The manual shortcut is Option+Space on Mac and Alt+Space on Windows. Drop the "Show HN" framing. Keep the limits. Title: saywhen: look at the screen, say the command, it can press Enter Use the Show HN body. Add this first line if the subreddit wants a personal lead: I have been using this on home days to talk to the agent in the terminal. [ONE_USE] Release notes Paste under the GitHub release. Replace the draft if the tag already has notes that overclaim. ## saywhen [VERSION] Look at the screen. Say the command. saywhen types it, and can press Enter. Beta for Mac and Windows. [MAC_STATUS]. Say "git status" to a terminal you chose. ### This build - [DATE] - [ONE_USE] ### Still true - Camera pictures are not saved and are not sent. - Audio is discarded after transcription unless you opt in to local tuning recordings. - Optional cloud cleanup stays off until you turn it on. - After the speech model download, dictation works offline.
